---
title: "Accounting for Reporting Delays in Public Health Surveillance"
---

Public health surveillance data are rarely complete when
first reported.
Cases, hospitalisations, and other events take time to be
confirmed, entered into databases, and reported to
central systems.
These **reporting delays** mean that the most recent data
systematically undercount the true number of events,
complicating real-time analysis.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false

weeks = Array.from({length: 74}, (_, i) => i + 1)

gaussian = (x, centre, spread, height) =>
  height * Math.exp(-0.5 * ((x - centre) / spread) ** 2)

syntheticRandom = seed => {
  const value = Math.sin(seed * 12.9898 + 78.233) * 43758.5453
  return value - Math.floor(value)
}

settlementWindow = i => {
  const group = syntheticRandom(i + 1)
  const draw = syntheticRandom(i + 101)
  if (group < 0.78) return 2 + Math.floor(draw * 7)
  if (group < 0.95) return 9 + Math.floor(draw * 18)
  return 27 + Math.floor(draw * 26)
}

finalData = weeks.map((week, i) => {
  const secondWave = gaussian(i, 43, 7.5, 1)
  const sampledEnd = settlementWindow(i)
  const revisionEndWeeks = secondWave > 0.25
    ? Math.max(10, Math.min(sampledEnd, 12))
    : Math.max(5, sampledEnd)
  return {
    week,
    series: "Finalized values",
    secondWave,
    revisionEndWeeks,
    tailWeight: 0.025 + 0.055 * secondWave +
      0.005 * syntheticRandom(i + 201),
    value: Math.round(
      34 +
      gaussian(i, 19, 5.5, 82) +
      gaussian(i, 43, 4.2, 205) +
      4 * Math.sin(i * 0.75) +
      2 * Math.cos(i * 0.27)
    )
  }
})

viewof figureControls = {
  const form = html`<form style="max-width: 760px;">
    <div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.35rem; font-weight: 600;">
      <label for="reporting-week">Data reported as of:</label>
      <output style="white-space: nowrap;"></output>
      <label style="display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.35rem; margin-left: 0.9rem;">
        <input class="nowcast-toggle" type="checkbox" aria-label="Show nowcasts">
        <span style="display: inline-block; width: 1.3rem; border-top: 3px dashed #7b3294;"></span>
        Show nowcasts
      </label>
    </div>
    <input
      id="reporting-week"
      type="range"
      min="0"
      max="${weeks.length - 1}"
      step="1"
      value="54"
      aria-label="Data reported as of"
      style="width: 100%;"
    >
  </form>`
  const input = form.querySelector("input[type='range']")
  const nowcast = form.querySelector(".nowcast-toggle")
  const output = form.querySelector("output")
  const update = () => {
    form.value = {
      asOf: Number(input.value),
      showNowcast: nowcast.checked
    }
    output.value = `Week ${form.value.asOf + 1}`
    form.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))
  }
  input.addEventListener("input", update)
  nowcast.addEventListener("input", update)
  update()
  return form
}

asOf = figureControls.asOf

showNowcast = figureControls.showNowcast
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false

reportedData = finalData
  .slice(0, asOf + 1)
  .map((d, i) => {
    const reportingAge = asOf - i + 1
    const fastProgress = (
      1 - Math.exp(-0.65 * Math.min(reportingAge, 5))
    ) / (1 - Math.exp(-0.65 * 5))
    let fraction = (1 - d.tailWeight) * fastProgress
    if (reportingAge >= d.revisionEndWeeks) {
      fraction = 1
    } else if (reportingAge > 5) {
      const tailProgress = (reportingAge - 5) /
        (d.revisionEndWeeks - 5)
      fraction = 1 - d.tailWeight *
        (1 - Math.pow(tailProgress, 0.8))
    }
    return {
      week: d.week,
      series: "Values reported by selected date",
      value: Math.round(d.value * fraction)
    }
  })

nowcastData = reportedData
  .slice(-6)
  .map(d => {
    const i = d.week - 1
    const reportingAge = asOf - i + 1
    const finalValue = finalData[i].value
    const laggedValue = (
      finalData[Math.max(0, i - 1)].value +
      finalData[Math.max(0, i - 2)].value +
      finalData[Math.max(0, i - 3)].value
    ) / 3
    const previousValue = finalData[Math.max(0, i - 1)].value
    const previousPreviousValue = finalData[Math.max(0, i - 2)].value
    const currentChange = finalValue - previousValue
    const previousChange = previousValue - previousPreviousValue
    const turningPoint = Math.min(
      1,
      Math.abs(currentChange - previousChange) / 12
    )
    const recency = (6 - reportingAge) / 5
    const firstWaveDifficulty = gaussian(i, 19, 5.5, 1)
    const difficulty = finalData[i].secondWave
    const lagWeight = Math.min(
      0.92,
      (0.18 + 0.52 * firstWaveDifficulty + 0.68 * difficulty +
        0.10 * turningPoint +
        0.28 * difficulty * turningPoint) *
        (0.35 + 0.65 * recency)
    )
    const errorScale = 0.015 + 0.035 * recency +
      0.025 * firstWaveDifficulty * recency +
      0.06 * difficulty * recency +
      0.04 * turningPoint * (0.35 + 0.65 * difficulty) * recency
    const error = (syntheticRandom(i + 301) - 0.5) * 2 * errorScale
    const laggedEstimate = (
      (1 - lagWeight) * finalValue + lagWeight * laggedValue
    ) * (1 + error)
    const reportedError = Math.abs(finalValue - d.value)
    const maximumErrorFraction = 0.18 +
      0.03 * difficulty - 0.09 * difficulty * turningPoint
    const maximumNowcastError = Math.floor(
      reportedError * maximumErrorFraction
    )
    const boundedEstimate = Math.max(
      finalValue - maximumNowcastError,
      Math.min(finalValue + maximumNowcastError, laggedEstimate)
    )
    const estimate = Math.max(
      d.value,
      Math.round(boundedEstimate)
    )
    const uncertainty = 0.05 +
      0.18 * Math.pow(recency, 1.2) +
      0.07 * difficulty * recency
    return {
      week: d.week,
      estimate,
      lower: Math.max(d.value, Math.round(estimate * (1 - uncertainty))),
      upper: Math.round(estimate * (1 + uncertainty))
    }
  })
```

```{ojs}
    Plot.lineY(finalData, {

        y: "estimate",

        strokeWidth: 2.5

      Plot.dot(nowcastData, {
        x: "week",
        y: "estimate",
        fill: "#7b3294",

        tip: true

    ] : []),
    Plot.ruleX([weeks[asOf]], {

```

Recent reported values can therefore give a misleading picture of what is
happening now, especially when reporting is severely incomplete.
Our goal is to help public health teams estimate the values that recent data
are likely to reach once more reports arrive and understand how uncertain
those estimates are.
This can help teams avoid mistaking reporting delays for real changes in
disease activity and support better situational awareness.

Several approaches can help public health teams work towards this goal.
This guide introduces the available options and focuses on practical guidance
for choosing and implementing methods in STLT settings, with emphasis on
adoption, communication, and real-world case studies.
It is intended as a companion to a technical overview of nowcasting methods
that covers mathematical formulation and computational properties in detail.

## Who is this for?

- **Epidemiologists and other state, tribal, local, and territorial (STLT)
  public health practitioners in the United States** working with delayed
  surveillance data and other real-time data issues.
- **Modellers and analysts** expanding their understanding of reporting delays
  and the methods available to address them.
- **Staff in healthcare facilities, laboratories, and other reporting
  organisations** seeking to understand how reporting processes affect
  downstream surveillance analyses.

## What this guide covers

- **Challenges** that arise when using surveillance data in
  real time, including reporting delays, data revisions,
  and site drop-in and drop-out.
- **Modelling approaches** that can adjust for reporting
  delays, from chain-ladder approaches to Bayesian
  hierarchical models.
- **A decision tree** to help select an appropriate method
  based on your data characteristics and use case.
- **A how-to guide** covering the common steps from
  assessing data through to communicating results.
- **Case studies** demonstrating practical implementations
  in surveillance settings.

## Get involved

This is a collaborative effort.
